codes.meaning: The freezer section is warming up past a safe point, so food stored there may be starting to thaw.
The unit experienced a power interruption at some point and settings may need to be re-confirmed.
The icemaker isn't cycling normally and should be inspected.
The unit is running in a showroom/demo setting, where lights and buttons stay active but cooling is intentionally turned off.
The automatic defrost cycle failed to complete successfully within the last day.
The fridge compartment's actual temperature doesn't match what the dial or display is set to.
The touch keypad is malfunctioning and will most likely need to be swapped out.
The oven cavity heated beyond its allowed temperature ceiling for a reason the control board couldn't identify.
The probe that measures oven temperature has failed and needs replacement.

F3.what_it_means: The probe that measures oven temperature has failed.
F3.why_it_happens: A sensor failure, so the control is working from a reading it cannot trust.
F3.what_to_try: Nothing here is an owner check — the probe is inside the oven cavity wall.
F3.when_to_call: When you see it. An oven working from a false temperature will not cook predictably.

codes.meaning: The main electronic control board itself is the component that has failed.
A part within the oven door's latching/locking mechanism has stopped working correctly.

F9.what_it_means: A part of the oven door's latching and locking mechanism has stopped working correctly.
F9.why_it_happens: Usually wear in the latch motor or its switch, often first noticed after a self-clean cycle.
F9.what_to_try: Check nothing is obstructing the door latch. That is the only owner-side cause to rule out.
F9.when_to_call: If the latch is clear and still will not operate, the mechanism needs replacing.

codes.meaning: Either the meat probe or the jack it plugs into has gone bad and needs replacing.
The oven temperature sensor has failed and needs replacing.
The electronic control itself has failed and needs replacing.
A problem in the upper cooling fan circuit, or the fan is physically obstructed.

F350.what_it_means: A problem in the upper cooling fan circuit, or the fan is physically obstructed.
F350.why_it_happens: Either the fan has failed or something is blocking it from turning freely.
F350.what_to_try: Check the vents around the oven are clear and nothing is obstructing airflow.
F350.when_to_call: If the vents are clear and the code stays, the fan or its circuit needs testing.

codes.meaning: A component in the door-lock circuit has failed.
The electronic control has failed and needs replacing.
The child lockout feature is switched on, so the controls will not respond.

LOC.what_it_means: Not a fault — the child lockout feature is switched on, so the controls will not respond.
LOC.why_it_happens: Easily switched on by accident, and often set deliberately and then forgotten.
LOC.what_to_try: Hold the lock pad, usually marked with a padlock, for a few seconds to release it.
LOC.when_to_call: Only if the lockout will not release, which points at the control panel.

codes.meaning: An invalid entry was made while setting the oven controls.
The oven is still too hot to begin a self-clean, or has not finished cooling from one.
One of the control panel buttons has been held down continuously for more than 30 seconds.
The temperature-sensing thermistor has short-circuited internally.
The temperature-sensing thermistor's circuit has an open break in it.
The touch keypad is malfunctioning and will most likely need replacement.
The oven cavity heated beyond its allowed temperature ceiling for an unidentified reason.
The oven-temperature probe has failed and needs replacement.
The main electronic control board is the failed component.
A part within the oven door's latching/locking mechanism has stopped working correctly.
Either the meat probe or its jack has gone bad.
The oven temperature sensor has failed and needs replacing.
The electronic control itself has failed and needs replacing.
A problem in the upper cooling fan circuit, or the fan is physically obstructed.
A component in the door-lock circuit has failed.
The electronic control has failed and needs replacing.
The child lockout feature is switched on, so the controls will not respond.
An invalid entry was made while setting the oven controls.
The oven is still too hot to begin a self-clean, or has not finished cooling from one.

cooktop.note: GE documents that digital cooktop controls DO display FXX fault codes, and then deliberately does not publish what they mean -- its own guidance is that an FXX code needs a trained service technician. There is no list to paraphrase. GE does publish a separate range/wall-oven code list, which is already recorded under ge.oven and ge.range.

dishwasher.note: GE states plainly that most dishwasher fault codes need a technician, and that a power-cycle at the breaker clears some of them. Codes are not present on every model. Codes are ordered by measured search demand first so the most-searched ones survive a block's ec_max cap; the plugin takes the first N in array order.

codes.meaning: Failure to drain — water is not leaving the machine.

FTD.what_it_means: The dishwasher has given up trying to drain and is telling you the water is not going anywhere.
FTD.why_it_happens: The usual three: a clogged air gap, a kinked or poorly routed drain hose, or a disposer holding debris where the dishwasher line joins it.
FTD.what_to_try: Check the air gap, then the drain hose behind or under the machine, then run the disposer. Clear standing water from the tub bottom before restarting.
FTD.when_to_call: If all three are clear and water still will not leave, the drain pump needs testing.

codes.meaning: Not a fault — the dishwasher is in Delay Start and counting down the hours before it begins.

1H.what_it_means: Nothing is wrong. Delay Start is switched on and the number in front of the H is how many hours remain before the cycle begins.
1H.why_it_happens: It is easy to set by accident, and it is often deliberately set to run overnight and then forgotten about.
1H.what_to_try: Cancel the delay — on most models holding the Start pad for a few seconds clears it — then select your cycle and start normally.
1H.when_to_call: No call needed. This is a setting, not a fault.

codes.meaning: The leak-detection system has sensed water where it should not be and stopped the machine.

LEAK DETECTED.what_it_means: A sensor has found water outside the tub and shut the dishwasher down to stop it spreading.
LEAK DETECTED.why_it_happens: Something above the base is leaking — a seal, a hose connection, or the tub. The message is the safety system working, not the fault itself.
LEAK DETECTED.what_to_try: Stop using the machine and turn its water supply off at the valve. The code tells you water is escaping but not from where.
LEAK DETECTED.when_to_call: This needs a technician — tracing the source means getting under or behind the machine.

codes.meaning: Draining has run past two minutes, so the machine has flagged a slow pump-out.

C1.what_it_means: The dishwasher tried to pump out and the drain took longer than the two minutes it allows.
C1.why_it_happens: Normally a restriction rather than a failure — a clogged air gap on the worktop, a drain hose that is kinked or badly positioned, or a disposer that has not been run and is holding debris in the line.
C1.what_to_try: Clean the air gap if your sink has one, check the drain hose for kinks, and run the disposer to clear it. Those are the three points GE names and all three are reachable.
C1.when_to_call: If the line is clear and it still drains slowly, the pump needs looking at.

codes.meaning: The whole pump-out cycle has exceeded seven minutes.
The dishwasher will not drain at all.
The machine filled twice after a power failure, which points at a float switch stuck or failed.
The pump-out finished faster than it should have, suggesting there was less water to move than expected.
Incoming water is too cool — GE expects at least 120°F at the dishwasher.
The water temperature sensor circuit has stopped working, so the control cannot tell how hot the water is.
The detergent cup is blocked and cannot open fully during the cycle.
Not a fault — the dishwasher lost power mid-cycle and is reporting the interruption.
The detergent cup has been left open rather than latched shut.
A low-water condition — the machine is not getting as much water as the cycle needs.
Either a possible leak or a control that needs resetting — GE lists both causes for this one.
The pressure sensor is sending the control a signal it cannot make sense of.

washer.note: GE publishes no general washer error-code list. Its Harmony washer support page documents only a generic "a problem has been detected with this unit" message with no codes behind it. Real GE washer codes do exist (353 for a lint filter clogged with softener residue, 18 for a pump filter needing cleaning, plus several consumer-help messages) but they belong specifically to the Profile UltraFast Combo washer/dryer. Publishing those under a "GE Washer" heading would show combo-only faults to top-loader and front-loader owners, so they are deliberately not recorded here.
washer.lead: Profile UltraFast Combo codes are real and sourced. If a ge-combo-washer-dryer page is ever built they belong on it, not on the general washer page.
